minutes.headline: ZBA approved a special permit for a four-story self-storage facility at 30 Summer Street.
minutes.summary:
The Zoning Board of Appeals held a public hearing on Safe Store Real Estate Company's application for a special permit to build a climate-controlled self-storage facility at 30 Summer Street, replacing a former auto dealership. The applicant's engineer presented site, parking, lighting, and fire department details, the board asked questions on height, materials, use classification, and buffering, and then voted to approve the special permit for the use before adjourning.</parameter>

what_happened.line: The Zoning Board of Appeals voted to approve a special permit for a four-story self-storage facility at 30 Summer Street.
The board chose not to table the matter for planning board review first, saying only the use, not dimensional requirements, was before it.
No members of the public attended the hearing, so no public comment was taken on the project.

why_it_matters: The permit lets a former auto dealership become a four-story storage building, a land-use change residents nearby may notice in scale and traffic.
The applicant's claim that the project will raise the property's tax revenue comes from its own petition materials and has not been verified by the town.
